ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A small ball is thrown horizontally from a height of $h=5\mathrm{m}$ above the ground with an initial velocity of $v_{0}=10\mathrm{m}/s$. Neglecting air resistance ($g$ is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$), find:

1. The time the small ball spends flying in the air
2. The horizontal distance from the landing point of the small ball to the throwing point.
3. The speed of the small ball when it hits the ground
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
$1\mathrm{s}$
$10\mathrm{m}$
$14.1\mathrm{m/s}$, at an angle of $45^\circ$ downward from the horizontal.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A small ball is thrown horizontally from a height of $h=5\mathrm{m}$ above the ground with an initial velocity of $v_{0}=10\mathrm{m}/s$. Neglecting air resistance ($g$ is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$), find: 1. The time the small ball spends flying in the air 2. The horizontal distance from the landing point of the small ball to the throwing point. 3. The speed of the small ball when it hits the ground
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: $1\mathrm{s}$ $10\mathrm{m}$ $14.1\mathrm{m/s}$, at an angle of $45^\circ$ downward from the horizontal
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Given h = 5 m, horizontal initial speed v0 = 10 m/s, and g = 10 m/s^2. Because the ball is thrown horizontally, its initial vertical velocity is 0. For the vertical motion, the falling distance is h = (1/2)gt^2, so 5 = (1/2)(10)t^2 = 5t^2. Hence t^2 = 1 and t = 1 s. Horizontally there is no acceleration, so the horizontal speed remains 10 m/s and the horizontal distance is x = v0 t = 10 * 1 = 10 m. At impact, the horizontal velocity is vx = 10 m/s and the vertical velocity is vy = gt = 10 * 1 = 10 m/s downward. Therefore the impact speed is v = sqrt(vx^2 + vy^2) = sqrt(10^2 + 10^2) = sqrt(200) ≈ 14.1 m/s. The direction is arctan(vy/vx) = arctan(10/10) = 45 degrees downward from the horizontal.
